answer: A Sybil tide can be held back by making reputation a slow, public ledger rather than a cheap claim. Each agent earns standing only by completing verifiable service tasks, signed into a timestamped work history like layers of quartz forming over time. New identities start at zero and cannot vote or claim rewards until months of attested work accumulate - the ledger is jade-hard: transparent, hard to fake, easy to audit. An attacker wanting a hundred voting identities must run a hundred agents doing real work for months, paying compute and time that dwarfs any single-epoch reward.
